title: a dynamic import whose specifier is computed cannot be shown to reach a trusted target, so it is refused
notes: The module-initialization trust claim is read off the resolved target's own declaration text, so a specifier that is not a literal resolves to no target and no claim can be found. Refusing it is the fail-closed answer and the only available one: the alternative is to admit an edge whose target is unknown until run time, which is precisely the hazard SMITHERS1510 names. This is the boundary of the dynamic-import family — the three literal-specifier targets are pinned beside it — and it is the form the reference used to compile and then die on at run time. 23-asset-imports/a-non-literal-dynamic-asset-import-is-rejected is the same principle for the asset loader, which is deliberately excluded from this rule on both backends.
